hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decisi.title: 品牌合同快到期，续约、换牌还是独立经营？酒店业主该怎样决策？
hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decisi.titleEn: When a Brand Contract Is Near Expiry, How Should a Hotel Owner Decide Among Renewal, Reflagging and Independent Operation?
hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decisi.description: 品牌合同临近届满，业主要先核对两件事：自己有没有权换牌，合同写明的提前通知日过了没有。这两件事没有核对完，续约、换牌和独立经营还不能放在一起比。牌子近来好不好、改造报价高不高，都排在后面。
hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decisi.descriptionEn: As a brand contract nears expiry, the owner should first check two things: whether the owner has authority to change the brand, and whether the advance-notice date written in the contract has already passed. Until both have been checked, renewal, reflagging and independent operation cannot be compared side by side. How the brand has been booking lately, and how high the renovation quotes are, come after that.
hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decisi.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 品牌合同临近届满，业主要先核对两件事：自己有没有权换牌，合同写明的提前通知日过了没有。这两件事没有核对完，续约、换牌和独立经营还不能放在一起比。牌子近来好不好、改造报价高不高，都排在后面。
业主会常常先谈预订，或者先让工程报一版客房和公区改造。合同里先要翻开的是另一页：续约须提前多少天书面提出，换牌要不要贷款人同意，摘牌之后中央预订和会员从哪一天停。这几项对不上，后面的报价没有比较基础。

品牌使用费、市场推广费、中央预订费如何加总，以及换牌时合同表面看不出来的开支，分别在[《摘牌、换牌还是独立经营：酒店业主如何算清品牌合同的全口径成本》](/zh/knowledge/hotel-brand-contract-total-cost-2026-09-14)和[《翻牌加盟前最该算清的3笔隐形成本》](/zh/lean/article/hotel-franchise-three-hidden-costs-2026-06-18)。这里不写某一家酒店的赔偿金额，也不写改造造价。合同里没有的数字，就空着。
一、委托管理和特许经营，拍板的人不是同一个
国内酒店挂牌，常见委托管理和特许经营。两种合同的权责差得很远，能拍板的人也不同。
委托管理是品牌方派人管店。业主付基本管理费，达到约定业绩后再付奖励管理费。年度预算和资本性支出往往要业主批准，总经理等关键岗位由谁任命，合同里通常写得很具体。业主容易觉得店是自己的，牌子想换就换。实际经常换不动：管理期限还在，业绩测试还没触发，或者换牌必须品牌方和贷款人同时同意。
特许经营则是品牌方许可使用品牌、品牌标准和中央系统，一般不直接雇用酒店的人。日常经营由业主或业主聘请的团队负责。品牌使用费多按客房收入计提，市场推广、中央预订和会员计划的费用另计。人是业主的，系统和会员多半不是。摘牌那天工牌可以换，客史、积分和渠道账号往往还在品牌方那里。
比较三条路之前，先看这份合同让谁有权结束、谁有权续，以及谁的同意还没拿到。贷款协议若把变更品牌写成须贷款人同意的事项，同意函没到，换牌和独立经营都还不是选项。股东协议若把品牌事项留给某一股东，业主会也不能代他表决。
法律上只剩一条路，材料就只准备这一条。再写出另外两条，会上像是在选择，选项却是假的。
二、续约看的是提前通知，不是到期当天
不少业主把到期日当成重新谈判的日子。合同常常把这天往前挪，并写明通知方式：书面、送给谁、提前多少天。过了这一天，续约选择权可能已经没有了，品牌方并无义务再坐下来谈。也有合同把续约选择权留在品牌方一边。到期当天，业主并不当然同时拥有离开和留下的权利。

希尔顿全球控股在截至2025年12月31日的年度报告里，写的是它自己的常见安排，不是某一家国内酒店的条款。新店的特许经营，初始期限通常约20年；从其他品牌或独立酒店转进来的，通常约10到20年。到期后可以再许可，续展一般约10到15年，由公司行使、加盟方行使，或双方约定，以具体合同为准。国内合同的年限和通知天数都可以不同，上面的年数不能直接抄进来。到期是否续约，要看选择权有没有被行使，不是日历走到最后一天就自动发生。
会上先核对的是通知截止日，不是合同到期日。截止日在文件里对不上，换牌报价先放一放。报价可以下周再要，通知日错过就补不回来。
三、三条路必须对着同一份合同看
续约、换牌、独立经营可以写在同一张纸上，每一项却要问同一件事。续约在谈年限，换牌在谈改造，独立经营在谈以后能省下多少品牌使用费，三列数字一加，比的就不是一个问题。
期限和通知先对齐。续约看选择权在品牌方、业主，还是双方都要同意，以及提前多少天、用什么方式提出。换牌要分清现有合同是在正常到期时结束，还是在业主提前终止、品牌方因违约解除时结束，并写上新品牌从哪一天承担中央预订和品牌标准。独立经营要写明店名、标识和渠道从哪一天停止使用。
品牌方、贷款人、股东的同意分开记。没有函件，就写尚未取得，不要写成问题不大。
终止赔偿只记什么情况下要付，不先填金额。到期后不再续约，业主主动提前解约，品牌方因欠费或达不到品牌标准而解除，三件事在合同里经常不是同一笔钱，有的根本不产生赔偿。合同没写金额的，空着。别的酒店听来的几个月品牌使用费，不要拿来填。
物业改造也不能三列共用一个数。续约时，品牌方往往要求按现行品牌标准重做一批客房和公区。换牌是新品牌自己的改造要求。独立经营可以不做品牌工程，但原先为了达标已经列进预算的项目，仍要逐项看还做不做。
中央预订、会员积分、客史、尚未入住的订单和协议客户价，要写结束日交给谁，哪些必须停用。独立经营这一列最容易只记省下来的品牌使用费，渠道和会员从哪一天起不再属于这家店，却空着。
委托管理还要把总经理的任命权写清楚。特许经营不要照抄这一栏，品牌方通常不是雇主。两栏写成一样，管理费和品牌使用费就会被谈成一回事。
某一项对得上合同正文和补充协议，可以拿到会上。缺补充协议或同意函的，标明待补，不参加这一次的比较。这条路在合同里已经走不通，整列拿掉，不必为了整齐留着。
四、品牌使用费、改造和终止赔偿，不是一笔账
会上常有人要一个总数：留下要花多少，离开要赔多少，换成另一个牌子开业前还要投多少。三笔钱管的事情不一样。品牌使用费是继续使用名称和系统的对价。改造看的是物业能不能达到品牌标准。终止赔偿是在某种解除条件下要不要付钱。加在一起，某条路会显得特别贵，或者特别省，其实是把不同的账加在了一起。
希尔顿那份年报把这几件事分开写，可以对照条款类型，不能拿来抄数。加盟店要完成物业改造计划，才能继续留在体系里。品牌方可以在约定的违约情形下终止特许经营，例如不付费、不符合品牌标准。因为加盟方违约而终止的，加盟方要按合同支付约定赔偿。年报没有给出一个所有酒店通用的赔偿额，也没有把到期不续写成同一笔赔偿。
费用同样分开列。特许经营的品牌使用费，通常按每月客房总收入的一定比例计收，有的还覆盖餐饮和其他收入。市场推广、技术和中央预订，一般另按销售或使用情况计费，会员计划另有费用。年报列出的是费用类别。自家合同的比例、含不含餐、推广费按什么基数，只能从合同和品牌对账单上抄。
委托管理也不能套特许经营的年限。年报里，管理合同初始期限通常是20到30年，延期怎么行使由谈判约定。部分合同设有业绩测试，看酒店自己的业绩，或和约定的竞争群比。达不到时，业主可以提前终止。品牌方常常有权把差额补上，有的合同则限制了这项权利。这些内容说明选择权写在哪里，不是一组可以填进国内合同的年数。
五、通知日对上之前，会不要表决
业主或资产负责人把合同、补充协议，以及贷款协议里有关变更品牌的条款，归到一张纸上。法务核对通知、终止和同意。财务核对品牌使用费、管理费和已经入账的系统费用。总经理只讲店里的事：中央预订和会员现在谁在操作，协议客户和在手订单的价格承诺到哪一天，总经理的任命权实际在谁手里。
会上先定通知截止日是哪一天，以及哪一项还缺文件、要向谁要同意。该填的还空着，就不要表决续约、换牌或摘牌。
合同期还长，又没有提前终止的条款，这张纸也不是用来推动现在摘牌的。新品牌的报价可以先收着，等现有合同的通知日和同意权核完再打开。
这些条款核完，还要算钱，再去看品牌成本的总账，以及换牌时那些不容易看见的开支。顺序反了，算出来的只是几条可能已经走不通的路的造价。
迈创兄弟C&T可以帮业主把通知、同意、终止、改造和系统交接整理到同一页上，交给法务和财务核对。结论仍以合同原文和律师意见为准。
contentEn: As a brand contract nears expiry, the owner should first check two things: whether the owner has authority to change the brand, and whether the advance-notice date written in the contract has already passed. Until both have been checked, renewal, reflagging and independent operation cannot be compared side by side. How the brand has been booking lately, and how high the renovation quotes are, come after that.

An owners' meeting often starts with bookings, or with a first engineering quote for guest rooms and public areas. The page to open first is a different one: how many days' written notice renewal requires, whether reflagging needs the lender's consent, and from which day central reservations and the loyalty programme stop after the brand comes off. If those items do not line up, later quotes have no basis for comparison.

How the brand fee, the marketing fee and the central-reservation fee add up, and the reflagging costs that do not appear on the face of the contract, are treated separately in [Leave the Brand, Rebrand, or Stay Independent: How Hotel Owners Should Calculate the Full Cost of a Brand Contract](/en/knowledge/hotel-brand-contract-total-cost-2026-09-14) and in [Three Hidden Costs to Calculate Before Hotel Franchise Conversion](/en/lean/article/hotel-franchise-three-hidden-costs-2026-06-18). This article does not state any one hotel's termination payment or renovation cost. Where the contract gives no figure, leave it blank.
## Management contracts and franchise agreements are not decided by the same person
Hotels in China commonly carry a brand under a management contract or a franchise agreement. The rights and duties differ widely, and so does the person who can decide.

Under a management contract, the brand company sends people to run the hotel. The owner pays a base management fee and, once the agreed performance is reached, an incentive management fee. The annual budget and capital expenditure often need the owner's approval, and the contract usually states in detail who appoints the general manager and other key positions. An owner can easily feel that the hotel is theirs and that the brand can be changed at will. In practice it often cannot: the management term is still running, a performance test has not been triggered, or a change of brand requires the consent of both the brand company and the lender.

A franchise is a different arrangement. The brand company licenses the brand, the brand standards and the central systems, and generally does not employ the hotel's staff directly. Day-to-day operation sits with the owner or with a team the owner engages. The brand fee is often charged on room revenue, while marketing, central reservations and the loyalty programme are charged separately. The people are the owner's. The systems and the members usually are not. On the day the brand comes off, name badges can be changed, but guest history, points and channel accounts often remain with the brand company.

Before comparing the three paths, see who this contract allows to end it, who may renew it, and whose consent is still missing. If the loan agreement makes a change of brand subject to the lender's consent, then until that consent arrives, reflagging and independent operation are not yet options. If a shareholders' agreement reserves brand matters to one shareholder, the owners' meeting cannot vote in that shareholder's place.
If the law leaves only one path, prepare materials for that path only. Writing out two further paths makes the meeting look like a choice whose options are not real.
## Renewal turns on advance notice, not on the expiry date itself

Many owners treat the expiry date as the day to renegotiate. The contract often moves that day forward and specifies how notice must be given: in writing, to whom, and how many days ahead. Once that date has passed, the option to renew may already be gone, and the brand company is under no obligation to sit down and talk again. Some contracts leave the renewal option with the brand company. On the expiry date, the owner does not automatically hold both the right to leave and the right to stay.

In its annual report for the year ended 31 December 2025, Hilton Worldwide Holdings describes its own usual arrangements, not the terms of any one hotel in China. For a new hotel, the initial franchise term is generally about 20 years. For a hotel converting from another brand or from independent operation, it is generally about 10 to 20 years. After expiry the franchise may be relicensed, generally for about 10 to 15 years, exercised by the company, by the franchisee, or as the two sides agree, according to the particular contract. The term and the number of notice days in a domestic contract can both differ, and the years above cannot be copied in. Whether the arrangement renews at expiry depends on whether the option is exercised. It does not happen automatically because the calendar has reached the last day.

The date to check first in the meeting is the notice deadline, not the contract expiry date. If the deadline cannot be matched in the documents, set the reflagging quotes aside. A quote can be asked for next week. A missed notice date cannot be made up.
## The three paths must be read against the same contract

Renewal, reflagging and independent operation can be written on one sheet, but each line must ask the same question. If renewal is discussed in years, reflagging in renovation, and independent operation in how much brand fee might later be saved, adding the three columns is not a comparison of one question.

Align term and notice first. For renewal, see whether the option sits with the brand company, with the owner, or requires both to agree, and how many days' notice is required and in what form. For reflagging, distinguish whether the existing contract ends at ordinary expiry, on the owner's early termination, or when the brand company terminates for default, and write the date from which the new brand takes on central reservations and brand standards. For independent operation, state the date from which the hotel name, the marks and the channels must stop being used.
Record the consent of the brand company, the lender and the shareholders separately. If there is no letter, write that it has not yet been obtained. Do not write that the point is a small one.

For a termination payment, record only the conditions on which it is payable. Do not fill in an amount first. Non-renewal after expiry, early termination by the owner, and termination by the brand company for unpaid fees or failure to meet brand standards are often not the same sum in the contract. Some of them give rise to no compensation at all. If the contract states no amount, leave it blank. Do not fill the blank with several months of brand fees heard from another hotel.

Renovation cannot share one figure across the three columns either. On renewal, the brand company often requires a set of guest rooms and public areas to be redone to the current brand standard. Reflagging brings the new brand's own renovation requirements. Independent operation can forgo brand works, but items already put into the budget in order to meet the standard still have to be reviewed one by one, to decide whether they are still done.

For central reservations, loyalty points, guest history, reservations not yet in house, and contracted account rates, write who receives them on the end date and which of them must be switched off. The independent-operation column most easily records only the brand fee saved, while the date from which the channels and the loyalty programme no longer belong to the hotel is left blank.

A management contract must also state who has the right to appoint the general manager. Do not copy that cell into a franchise. The brand company is usually not the employer. If the two columns are written the same way, the management fee and the brand fee will be negotiated as if they were the same thing.

An item that matches the body of the contract and the supplemental agreements can go to the meeting. If a supplemental agreement or a consent letter is missing, mark it as still to be obtained and leave it out of this round of comparison. If a path is already closed in the contract, take the whole column off. Do not keep it so that the sheet looks tidy.
## The brand fee, renovation and a termination payment are not one account

Someone in the meeting often asks for a single total: what it costs to stay, what must be paid in order to leave, and what must still be invested before opening under another brand. The three sums govern different things. The brand fee is the consideration for continuing to use the name and the systems. Renovation asks whether the property can meet the brand standard. A termination payment asks whether money is due under a particular termination condition. Added together, one path can look especially expensive, or especially cheap, because different accounts have been added into one.

Hilton's annual report sets these matters out separately. It can be used to compare types of clause. It cannot be used to copy figures. A franchised hotel must complete a property improvement plan in order to remain in the system. The brand company may terminate the franchise in agreed events of default, for example non-payment or a failure to meet brand standards. Where the franchise ends because of the franchisee's default, the franchisee must pay the compensation agreed in the contract. The annual report does not give one amount of compensation for every hotel, and it does not treat a decision not to renew at expiry as that same compensation.

The fees are listed separately as well. A franchise brand fee is generally charged as a percentage of monthly gross rooms revenue, and in some cases it also covers food and beverage and other revenue. Marketing, technology and central reservations are generally charged separately according to sales or usage, and the loyalty programme carries a further fee. The annual report lists the categories of fee. The percentage in the hotel's own contract, whether food and beverage is included, and the base used for the marketing fee can be taken only from the contract and from the brand's statements.

A management contract cannot borrow the term of a franchise either. In the annual report, the initial term of a management contract is generally 20 to 30 years, and how an extension is exercised is settled in negotiation. Some contracts include a performance test, looking at the hotel's own results or at an agreed competitive set. If the test is not met, the owner may terminate early. The brand company often has the right to make up the shortfall, and some contracts limit that right. These provisions show where the option is written. They are not a set of years that can be written into a domestic contract.
## Do not take a vote until the notice date has been matched

The owner, or the person responsible for the asset, should bring onto one sheet the contract, the supplemental agreements, and the clauses in the loan agreement that concern a change of brand. Legal checks notice, termination and consent. Finance checks the brand fee, the management fee and the system charges already booked. The general manager speaks only to what is happening in the hotel: who currently operates central reservations and the loyalty programme, until what date the rates promised to contracted accounts and to bookings in hand run, and who actually holds the right to appoint the general manager.

The meeting first settles which day the notice deadline falls on, and which item is still missing a document and whose consent must be asked for. If what still has to be filled in is blank, do not vote on renewal, reflagging or taking the brand off.

If the contract term still has a long way to run, and there is no early-termination clause, the sheet is not a means of pushing a de-flag now. Quotes from a new brand can be received and left unopened until the notice date and the consent rights under the existing contract have been checked.

Once those clauses have been checked, the money still has to be calculated, and the owner still has to look at the full account of brand cost and at the reflagging costs that are not easy to see. If that order is reversed, the figure produced is only the cost of paths that may already be closed.

MarvelBros C&T can help the owner set notice, consent, termination, renovation and the handover of systems out on one page, for legal and finance to check. The conclusion remains governed by the text of the contract and by legal advice.
